title: CBI questions per case type on Loss information
walkthroughSteps: Apply any AC: lands on FNOL Loss information with policy POL-2024-001 selected.
Tick Business interruption under Type of damage, answer Yes to the CBI question, then pick the case type the AC names.
AC-01 to AC-05 are one per CBI branch, AC-06 is switching case type, AC-07 is what the created section shows after submit.
Prototype ticket, no Jira of its own. Source: CBI functional design, Confluence 3163290837.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Supplier or Customer asks for the third party and where it happened
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** FNOL Loss information on policy POL-2024-001 (offers all 12 CBI case types). Tick **Business interruption** under Type of damage, answer **Yes** to the CBI question.

**Pick:** **Supplier: Named** (or any Supplier / Customer type).

**Try:** Press **Next** with the new fields empty: **Supplier name** and the originating location are required, **Supplier industry (optional)** is not. Pick a Customer type: the labels read Customer name / Customer industry. Unnamed types make the name optional.

Source: CBI functional design (Confluence 3163290837), Data Captured table. Industry stays a typed field: the design says manual entry only in baseline, no WB/AOC code list.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Denial of Access asks whether an authority ordered it
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** FNOL Loss information on policy POL-2024-001 (offers all 12 CBI case types). Tick **Business interruption** under Type of damage, answer **Yes** to the CBI question.

**Pick:** any of the 4 **Denial of Access** types.

**Try:** Only one extra question shows: **Was access denied by order of an authority?** Yes / No. Press **Next** without answering: **Answer required**, and the error summary names it.

Source: functional design, Category-specific fields (Authority order Y/N), and the UI/UX alignment page (3157631012), which lists all 4 Denial of Access types. The design still calls the mapping a hypothesis (Open Point 13).

**Pick:** **Loss of Attraction: With PD Trigger** or **Without PD Trigger**.

Open in the design: the functional design names a "Trigger event location" for Loss of Attraction but says it may be the same as the originating loss location and needs reconciling; the diagram asks "is this the Loss location captured? need use case". Nothing is built until that is decided.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: After submit, the Business interruption section shows the same answers
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** FNOL Loss information on policy POL-2024-001 (offers all 12 CBI case types). Tick **Business interruption** under Type of damage, answer **Yes** to the CBI question.

**Pick:** any case type and answer its fields. Then walk the wizard: on Entities & Damages tick an entity under Business interruption, and Submit claim.

**Try:** Open the new claim's **Sections**, the entity's menu, **View details**. Entity details shows the CBI case type, plus Supplier/Customer name, industry and Originating loss location (Supplier/Customer), or **Access denied by order of an authority** (Denial of Access), or **Utility type** (Service Interruption). Rows a case type does not ask for are not shown.

Not built: the diagram says the CBI section "includes Extension Limits". The design takes those limits from the policy per case type (Open Point 10) and gives no values, so the section shows none.
